# Shapes

Header: `winui/ui/media/Shape.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/media/Shape.hpp`.

The base of the shapes. A shape is one geometry, filled with [fill()](#fill) and outlined with [stroke()](#stroke), drawn with one [Renderer::draw_geometry()](../rendering/renderer.md#draw_geometry) call.

It can't be constructed on its own. Use [Rectangle](#uirectangle), [Ellipse](#uiellipse), [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) or [Path](#uipath), or their ui:: specs. Everything here is shared by all six. Shapes take no input and no focus.

Example: 
```cpp
auto shape = std::make_unique<ui::EllipseControl>();
shape->set_fill(ui::colors::White);
shape->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
shape->set_stroke_thickness(2.0f);
shape->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::Uniform); // a circle, whatever the slot's aspect
shape->set_width(100.0f);
shape->set_height(60.0f);
window.set_content(std::move(shape)); // drawn as one geometry: fill and stroke together
```

## `ui::Rectangle`

A rectangle, optionally with rounded corners. Builds a [ui::RectangleControl](#class-rectanglecontrol).

It has no natural size. Give it a [`.width`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec) and [`.height`](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec), or let the parent stretch it.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<ui::Color> swatch{ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF0078D4)};

window.set_content(ui::HorizontalStack{
    .spacing  = 12,
    .content  = {
        ui::Rectangle{ .fill = ui::colors::Black, .width = 100, .height = 60 },
        ui::Rectangle{ .fill             = swatch, // follows the property
                       .stroke           = ui::colors::Black,
                       .stroke_thickness = 2.0f,
                       .radius_x         = 8.0f,
                       .radius_y         = 8.0f,
                       .width            = 100,
                       .height           = 60 },
    },
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Rectangle{
    .fill, .stroke, .stroke_thickness, .stroke_style, .stretch, .radius_x, .radius_y, .style,
    .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uirectangle-fill"></span>`fill` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | The interior paint: a [Color](../core/color.md), gradient, acrylic or [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md). Empty paints none. |
| <span id="uirectangle-stroke"></span>`stroke` | `ui::Binding<ui::Paint>` |  | The outline paint. Empty draws no outline and reserves no room for one. |
| <span id="uirectangle-stroke_thickness"></span>`stroke_thickness` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{1.0f}` | The outline width, in DIPs. |
| <span id="uirectangle-stroke_style"></span>`stroke_style` | `ui::Binding<ui::StrokeStyle>` |  | Caps, join, miter limit and dashes. Its `thickness` is ignored for [`.stroke_thickness`](#uirectangle-stroke_thickness). |
| <span id="uirectangle-stretch"></span>`stretch` | `ui::Binding<ui::Stretch>` | `{ui::Stretch::Fill}` | How the shape fills its layout rect. [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill) by default. |
| <span id="uirectangle-radius_x"></span>`radius_x` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{0.0f}` | Horizontal corner radius in DIPs, clamped to half the width. 0 gives square corners. |
| <span id="uirectangle-radius_y"></span>`radius_y` | `ui::Binding<float>` | `{0.0f}` | Vertical corner radius in DIPs, clamped to half the height. 0 gives square corners. |

## `ui::Line`

A straight line from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2). Builds a [ui::LineControl](#class-linecontrol).

A line has no interior, so there is no `.fill`. Without a [`.stroke`](#uiline-stroke) it draws nothing.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<float> end_x{200.0f};

window.set_content(ui::Line{
    .x1               = 0.0f,
    .y1               = 50.0f,
    .x2               = end_x,
    .y2               = 50.0f,
    .stroke           = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFF4682B4),
    .stroke_thickness = 4.0f,
});
end_x = 300.0f; // the line follows
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Line{
    .x1, .y1, .x2, .y2, .stroke, .stroke_thickness, .stroke_style, .stretch, .style, .margin,
    .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

## `ui::Path`

Any geometry, with [`data`](#uipath-data) from [PathGeometry::parse()](../rendering/path-geometry.md#parse) or the [PathGeometry](../rendering/path-geometry.md) builders. Builds a [ui::PathControl](#class-pathcontrol).

[PathGeometry::parse()](../rendering/path-geometry.md#parse) returns nullopt for markup that doesn't parse. A literal known to be valid is usually dereferenced directly.

Example: 
```cpp
window.set_content(ui::Path{
    .data             = *ui::PathGeometry::parse("M 10,100 C 100,25 300,250 400,75 H 200"),
    .stroke           = ui::Color::from_argb(0xFFB8860B),
    .stroke_thickness = 3.0f,
});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::Path{
    .data, .fill, .stroke, .stroke_thickness, .stroke_style, .stretch, .style, .margin, .width,
    .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height, .horizontal_alignment,
    .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .accessibility, .on_pointer_entered,
    .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down, .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uipath-data"></span>`data` | `ui::Binding<ui::PathGeometry>` |  | The figures to draw, in local DIPs: `*PathGeometry::parse("M 0,0 L 10,10")` or a [PathGeometry](../rendering/path-geometry.md) builder. |

| <span id="uipath-stroke_style"></span>`stroke_style` | `ui::Binding<ui::StrokeStyle>` |  | Caps, join, miter limit and dashes. Its `thickness` is ignored for [`.stroke_thickness`](#uipath-stroke_thickness). |
| <span id="uipath-stretch"></span>`stretch` | `ui::Binding<ui::Stretch>` | `{ui::Stretch::None}` | How the geometry scales into the layout rect. None, the default, draws it where it is. |
| <span id="uipath-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uipath-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uipath-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uipath-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uipath-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uipath-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uipath-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::Path>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### build

```cpp
std::unique_ptr<Element> build()&&
```

Consumes the spec and returns the built [ui::PathControl](#class-pathcontrol); the caller owns it.

## `ui::Shape`

Derives from `ui::Element`.

The base of the shapes. A shape is one geometry, filled with [fill()](#fill) and outlined with [stroke()](#stroke), drawn with one [Renderer::draw_geometry()](../rendering/renderer.md#draw_geometry) call.

It can't be constructed on its own. Use [Rectangle](#uirectangle), [Ellipse](#uiellipse), [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) or [Path](#uipath), or their ui:: specs. Everything here is shared by all six. Shapes take no input and no focus.

Example: 
```cpp
auto shape = std::make_unique<ui::EllipseControl>();
shape->set_fill(ui::colors::White);
shape->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
shape->set_stroke_thickness(2.0f);
shape->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::Uniform); // a circle, whatever the slot's aspect
shape->set_width(100.0f);
shape->set_height(60.0f);
window.set_content(std::move(shape)); // drawn as one geometry: fill and stroke together
```

### fill

```cpp
const Paint& fill() const
```

The interior paint. Empty, the default, paints no interior.

### set_fill

```cpp
void set_fill(Paint paint)
```

Sets the interior paint: a [Color](../core/color.md), a gradient, an [AcrylicBrush](../rendering/acrylic-brush.md) or a [ThemeColor](../tree/theme-color.md). Redraws.

### stroke

```cpp
const Paint& stroke() const
```

The outline paint. Empty, the default, draws no outline and makes [`stroke_thickness()`](#stroke_thickness) count as zero for layout.

### set_stroke

```cpp
void set_stroke(Paint paint)
```

Sets the outline paint. Updates layout and redraws, since whether there is a stroke changes how much room the shape takes.

### stroke_thickness

```cpp
float stroke_thickness() const
```

The outline width, 1 by default. This is the `thickness` of [stroke_style()](#stroke_style). The other stroke settings, such as caps, join, miter limit and dashes, are in that [StrokeStyle](../rendering/stroke-style.md).

### set_stroke_thickness

```cpp
void set_stroke_thickness(float thickness)
```

Sets the outline width in DIPs. Updates layout and redraws, since the room the stroke takes changes with it.

### stroke_style

```cpp
const StrokeStyle& stroke_style() const
```

The whole pen, [stroke_thickness()](#stroke_thickness) included.

### set_stroke_style

```cpp
void set_stroke_style(const StrokeStyle& style)
```

Sets everything but the thickness, which [set_stroke_thickness()](#set_stroke_thickness) sets. Redraws.

### stretch

```cpp
Stretch stretch() const
```

How the geometry fills the layout rect. [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill) by default for [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse), None for the rest. For [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse), Uniform and UniformToFill make the outline square and None collapses it. For the other shapes it scales the geometry's bounds into the rect, less the stroke.

### set_stretch

```cpp
void set_stretch(Stretch stretch)
```

Sets the stretch. Updates layout and redraws.

### rendered_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry rendered_geometry() const
```

The geometry as drawn, in window coordinates, as [render()](../tree/element.md#render) passes it to the renderer. Valid after [arrange()](../tree/element.md#arrange).

### Shape

```cpp
Shape(Stretch stretch)
```

For the concrete shapes. [`stretch`](#stretch) is their default [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch).

### effective_stroke_thickness

```cpp
float effective_stroke_thickness() const
```

The thickness layout reserves: the absolute stroke thickness with a stroke, 0 without.

### natural_geometry

```cpp
virtual PathGeometry natural_geometry() const
```

For [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) and [Path](#uipath): the geometry in local coordinates, before any stretch. [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse) override [outline_geometry()](#outline_geometry) instead and never call this.

### stretches_geometry

```cpp
virtual bool stretches_geometry() const
```

Whether [stretch()](#stretch) scales the geometry. False for [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse), which build their geometry at the layout size themselves.

### outline_geometry

```cpp
virtual PathGeometry outline_geometry(Size) const
```

For [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse): the geometry, in local coordinates, for an element laid out at `size`.

### outline_rect

```cpp
Rect outline_rect(Size size, bool check_degenerate) const
```

The layout rect inset by half the stroke, then made square or collapsed as the stretch says. With `check_degenerate`, which [Rectangle](#uirectangle) sets, the full rect is kept when the stroke is as thick as a side.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The natural geometry's size under [stretch()](#stretch). With Stretch::None that is its bottom-right corner plus half the stroke, otherwise its bounds scaled into `available`. [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse) override this.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the geometry once with [fill()](#fill), [stroke()](#stroke) and [stroke_style()](#stroke_style). Draws nothing when both paints are unset or the shape was laid out with no area.

## class RectangleControl

Derives from `ui::Shape`.

A rectangle, optionally with elliptically rounded corners. [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) defaults to [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill).

Its geometry is built from its layout rect, inset by half the stroke, so without a width and height it fills the slot its parent gives it. The declarative form is [ui::Rectangle](#uirectangle).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* card = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::RectangleControl>());
card->set_fill(ui::Color::from_rgba(70, 130, 180));
card->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
card->set_stroke_thickness(2.0f);
card->set_radius_x(8.0f);
card->set_radius_y(8.0f);
card->set_width(120.0f);
card->set_height(80.0f);
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### RectangleControl

```cpp
RectangleControl()
```

A rectangle with Stretch::Fill and no fill or stroke. Set a [fill()](#fill) or [stroke()](#stroke) to see it.

### radius_x

```cpp
float radius_x() const
```

The corners' horizontal radius in DIPs. 0, the default, gives square corners.

### set_radius_x

```cpp
void set_radius_x(float radius)
```

Sets the horizontal corner radius. Redraws.

### radius_y

```cpp
float radius_y() const
```

The corners' vertical radius in DIPs. 0, the default, gives square corners.

### set_radius_y

```cpp
void set_radius_y(float radius)
```

Sets the vertical corner radius. Redraws.

### stretches_geometry

```cpp
bool stretches_geometry() const override
```

Whether [stretch()](#stretch) scales the geometry. False for [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse), which build their geometry at the layout size themselves.

### outline_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry outline_geometry(Size size) const override
```

For [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse): the geometry, in local coordinates, for an element laid out at `size`.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

No size of its own, so an explicit width and height apply. Under UniformToFill it asks for a square covering `available`.

## class EllipseControl

Derives from `ui::Shape`.

The ellipse inscribed in the outline rect. [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) defaults to [Fill](../layout/fill.md#uifill).

Like [Rectangle](#uirectangle), it takes its size from layout. Stretch::Uniform makes it a circle, placed at the rect's top-left. The declarative form is [ui::Ellipse](#uiellipse).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Horizontal);
auto* dot  = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::EllipseControl>());
dot->set_fill(ui::colors::White);
dot->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
dot->set_stroke_thickness(2.0f);
dot->set_width(48.0f);
dot->set_height(48.0f);
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### EllipseControl

```cpp
EllipseControl()
```

An ellipse with Stretch::Fill and no fill or stroke.

### stretches_geometry

```cpp
bool stretches_geometry() const override
```

Whether [stretch()](#stretch) scales the geometry. False for [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse), which build their geometry at the layout size themselves.

### outline_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry outline_geometry(Size size) const override
```

For [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse): the geometry, in local coordinates, for an element laid out at `size`.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

Like [Rectangle](#uirectangle)'s: no size of its own, except a covering square under UniformToFill.

## class LineControl

Derives from `ui::Shape`.

A line from (x1, y1) to (x2, y2) in local coordinates.

A line has no interior, so only [stroke()](#stroke) draws. With the default Stretch::None it asks for room up to its farther end plus half the stroke. The declarative form is [ui::Line](#uiline).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* rule = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::LineControl>(ui::Point{0.0f, 0.0f},
                                                      ui::Point{200.0f, 0.0f}));
rule->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
rule->set_stroke_thickness(2.0f);
rule->set_x2(300.0f); // stretch it later
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### LineControl

```cpp
LineControl()
```

A line from (0, 0) to (0, 0). Invisible until its ends and a stroke are set.

### LineControl

```cpp
LineControl(Point from, Point to)
```

A line from [`from`](#from) to [`to`](#to), in DIPs of local coordinates.

### from

```cpp
Point from() const
```

The start point, (x1, y1).

### to

```cpp
Point to() const
```

The end point, (x2, y2).

### set_x1

```cpp
void set_x1(float v)
```

Sets the start point's x. Each of the four setters updates layout and redraws.

### set_y1

```cpp
void set_y1(float v)
```

Sets the start point's y.

### set_x2

```cpp
void set_x2(float v)
```

Sets the end point's x.

### set_y2

```cpp
void set_y2(float v)
```

Sets the end point's y.

### natural_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry natural_geometry() const override
```

For [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) and [Path](#uipath): the geometry in local coordinates, before any stretch. [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse) override [outline_geometry()](#outline_geometry) instead and never call this.

## class PolylineControl

Derives from `ui::Shape`.

Straight segments through a list of points. The fill rule, EvenOdd by default, decides what counts as inside.

A [Polyline](#uipolyline) is open: its stroke stops at the last point. [Polygon](#uipolygon), which derives from it, closes the last point back to the first. The declarative form is [ui::Polyline](#uipolyline).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* zigzag = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::PolylineControl>(std::vector<ui::Point>{
    {10.0f, 200.0f}, {60.0f, 140.0f}, {130.0f, 140.0f}, {180.0f, 200.0f}}));
zigzag->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
zigzag->set_stroke_thickness(4.0f);
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### PolylineControl

```cpp
PolylineControl()
```

An empty polyline: draws nothing until it has points.

### PolylineControl

```cpp
PolylineControl(std::vector<Point> points)
```

A polyline through [`points`](#points), in local DIPs.

### points

```cpp
const std::vector<Point>& points() const
```

The points, in local coordinates.

### set_points

```cpp
void set_points(std::vector<Point> points)
```

Replaces every point. Updates layout and redraws.

### fill_rule

```cpp
FillRule fill_rule() const
```

Which enclosed areas the fill paints where segments cross.

### set_fill_rule

```cpp
void set_fill_rule(FillRule rule)
```

Sets the fill rule. Redraws.

### closed

```cpp
virtual bool closed() const
```

Whether the figure closes back to its first point. False here, true for [Polygon](#uipolygon).

### natural_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry natural_geometry() const override
```

For [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) and [Path](#uipath): the geometry in local coordinates, before any stretch. [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse) override [outline_geometry()](#outline_geometry) instead and never call this.

## class PolygonControl

Derives from `ui::PolylineControl`.

A [Polyline](#uipolyline) whose last point joins back to its first, so the stroke goes all the way around. The declarative form is [ui::Polygon](#uipolygon).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel    = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
auto* triangle = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::PolygonControl>(std::vector<ui::Point>{
    {10.0f, 110.0f}, {60.0f, 10.0f}, {110.0f, 110.0f}}));
triangle->set_fill(ui::colors::White);
triangle->set_stroke(ui::colors::Black);
triangle->set_fill_rule(ui::FillRule::Nonzero);
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### PolygonControl

```cpp
PolygonControl() = default
```

An empty polygon: draws nothing until it has points.

### PolygonControl

```cpp
PolygonControl(std::vector<Point> points)
```

A polygon through [`points`](#points), in local DIPs, closed back to the first.

### closed

```cpp
bool closed() const override
```

Whether the figure closes back to its first point. False here, true for [Polygon](#uipolygon).

## class PathControl

Derives from `ui::Shape`.

Any geometry, parsed from markup with [PathGeometry::parse()](../rendering/path-geometry.md#parse) or built with the [PathGeometry](../rendering/path-geometry.md) builders and [PathGeometry::group()](../rendering/path-geometry.md#group).

Stretch::None, the default, draws the geometry where its coordinates put it. Any other [Stretch](../rendering/namespace-ui.md#stretch) scales its bounds into the layout rect. The declarative form is [ui::Path](#uipath).

Example: 
```cpp
auto panel = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
if (auto arrow = ui::PathGeometry::parse("F1 M 20,20L 24,10L 24,24L 5,24")) // nullopt if malformed
{
    auto* icon = panel->add(std::make_unique<ui::PathControl>(std::move(*arrow)));
    icon->set_fill(ui::colors::Black);
    icon->set_stretch(ui::Stretch::Uniform);
    icon->set_width(32.0f);
    icon->set_height(32.0f);
}
window.set_content(std::move(panel));
```

### PathControl

```cpp
PathControl()
```

An empty path: draws nothing until it has [data()](#data).

### PathControl

```cpp
PathControl(PathGeometry data)
```

A path drawing [`data`](#data), in local coordinates.

### data

```cpp
const PathGeometry& data() const
```

The geometry, in local coordinates before any stretch.

### set_data

```cpp
void set_data(PathGeometry data)
```

Replaces the geometry. Updates layout and redraws.

### natural_geometry

```cpp
PathGeometry natural_geometry() const override
```

For [Line](#uiline), [Polyline](#uipolyline), [Polygon](#uipolygon) and [Path](#uipath): the geometry in local coordinates, before any stretch. [Rectangle](#uirectangle) and [Ellipse](#uiellipse) override [outline_geometry()](#outline_geometry) instead and never call this.
